description: Fires when the opponent has three of their stones stacked on top of column 1 (second column from the left) with the cell above empty, i.e. a vertical must-block in column 1; this gives very strong activation (20-70) regardless of other stones. A raised opponent vertical three in column 5 fires weakly. Vertical threes in other columns, and column-1 threats along rows or diagonals, do not fire. Many weak near-threshold firings have no clear pattern.
effect: Strongly active it puts nearly all move probability on column 1 (e.g. 0.01 -> 1.00 from a neutral position); ablating it on real column-1 threats changes nothing because the block is still chosen.
notes: Top bands (act>4, ~1% of positions) are almost entirely opponent vertical three in column 1 (precision 0.99 for that rule alone, F1 0.43). Adding raised col-5 vertical three: best F1 0.461 (P 0.81, R 0.32). Rejected: any must-block in col 1 (P 0.44), vertical three in any column (F1 0.29). About two thirds of firing is a weak, diffuse band just above the 0.766 threshold that I could not describe; steer shows it has no effect. Simulation share nan (ceiling ill-defined).
